title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 59 (Rectification of Register of Members)

content.overview: Section 59(1) provides that if the name of any person is, without sufficient cause, entered in the register of members of a company, or after having been entered is, without sufficient cause, omitted therefrom, or if a default is made or unnecessary delay takes place in entering in the register the fact of any person having become or ceased to be a member, the person aggrieved, or any member of the company, or the company may appeal in the prescribed form to the Tribunal, or to a competent court outside India specified by the Central Government by notification in respect of foreign members or debenture holders residing outside India, for rectification of the register. Section 59(2) empowers the Tribunal, after hearing the parties, either to dismiss the appeal or to direct that the transfer or transmission shall be registered by the company within ten days of receipt of the order, or to direct rectification of the records of the depository or the register and, in the latter case, to direct the company to pay damages, if any, sustained by the party aggrieved. Section 59(3) provides that the section does not restrict the right of a holder of securities to transfer such securities, and any person acquiring such securities is entitled to voting rights unless the voting rights have been suspended by an order of the Tribunal. Section 59(4) allows the Tribunal, on application by the depository, company, depository participant, holder of the securities or SEBI, to direct any company or depository to set right a transfer of securities made in contravention of the SCRA, the SEBI Act, this Act or any other law and to rectify its register or records.
content.glance: Tribunal (or notified foreign court for foreign members/debenture holders) may rectify register of members (or depository records) where name entered/omitted without sufficient cause or with default/delay; may direct registration within 10 days or damages; transfer right and voting rights preserved unless suspended; contravening transfers may be set right under s. 59(4).
content.study: If the name of any person is, without sufficient cause, entered in the register of members of a company, or after having been entered in the register is, without sufficient cause, omitted therefrom, or if a default is made or unnecessary delay takes place in entering in the register the fact of any person having become or ceased to be a member, the person aggrieved, or any member of the company, or the company may appeal in such form as may be prescribed to the Tribunal, or to a competent court outside India specified by the Central Government by notification in respect of foreign members or debenture holders residing outside India, for rectification of the register (s. 59(1)). The Tribunal may, after hearing the parties to the appeal under sub-section (1), by order either dismiss the appeal or direct that the transfer or transmission shall be registered by the company within a period of ten days of the receipt of the order or direct rectification of the records of the depository or the register and in the latter case direct the company to pay damages, if any, sustained by the party aggrieved (s. 59(2)). The provisions of this section shall not restrict the right of a holder of securities to transfer such securities and any person acquiring such securities shall be entitled to voting rights unless the voting rights have been suspended by an order of the Tribunal (s. 59(3)). Where the transfer of securities is in contravention of any of the provisions of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 or this Act or any other law for the time being in force, the Tribunal may, on an application made by the depository, company, depository participant, the holder of the securities or the Securities and Exchange Board, direct any company or a depository to set right the contravention and rectify its register or records concerned (s. 59(4)). Current-law framing: identify the register error, omission or delay; establish standing of the applicant; choose the correct forum (Tribunal or notified foreign court); seek the appropriate order under s. 59(2) or (4); note that transfer rights and voting rights continue unless suspended.

sections.heading: Grounds and standing (s. 59(1))
sections.body: Name entered or omitted without sufficient cause, or default or unnecessary delay in entering the fact of becoming or ceasing to be a member. Applicant: person aggrieved, any member, or the company. Forum: Tribunal, or competent court outside India specified by Central Government notification for foreign members or debenture holders residing outside India.

sections.heading: Tribunal orders (s. 59(2))
sections.body: After hearing, the Tribunal may dismiss the appeal, or direct registration of the transfer or transmission within ten days of receipt of the order, or direct rectification of the records of the depository or the register and, in the latter case, direct the company to pay damages sustained by the party aggrieved.

sections.heading: Transfer and voting rights preserved (s. 59(3))
sections.body: The section does not restrict the right of a holder of securities to transfer such securities. Any person acquiring such securities is entitled to voting rights unless the voting rights have been suspended by an order of the Tribunal.

sections.heading: Contravening transfers (s. 59(4))
sections.body: Where transfer of securities contravenes the SCRA, the SEBI Act, this Act or any other law, the Tribunal may, on application by the depository, company, depository participant, holder of the securities or SEBI, direct the company or depository to set right the contravention and rectify its register or records.

examples.title: Wrongful omission
examples.body: A transferee’s name is omitted from the register without sufficient cause. The transferee applies under s. 59(1) for rectification and, if sustained, damages under s. 59(2).

examples.title: Delay in registration of transmission
examples.body: Unnecessary delay in entering a transmission on death leads the legal representative to seek rectification under s. 59(1). The Tribunal may direct registration within ten days or order rectification and damages.

examples.title: Contravening transfer
examples.body: A transfer of securities is alleged to contravene the SCRA. SEBI or the depository applies under s. 59(4) for an order directing the company or depository to set right the contravention and rectify the register or records.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 59 limited to the register of members kept by the company?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 59(2) expressly permits the Tribunal to direct rectification of the records of the depository or the register. Section 59(1) also contemplates a competent court outside India for foreign members or debenture holders.

hypotheticals.question: Does an application under s. 59 suspend the right to transfer or voting rights?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 59(3) provides that the section does not restrict the right of a holder of securities to transfer such securities, and any person acquiring such securities is entitled to voting rights unless the voting rights have been suspended by an order of the Tribunal.

distinctions.title: Rectification (s. 59) vs refusal of registration and appeal (s. 58)
distinctions.left: Correcting the register (or depository records) after entry, omission or delay; damages and 10-day registration direction available
distinctions.right: Challenging the company’s refusal to register a transfer or transmission within the statutory time; appeal route under s. 58

misconceptions.trap: Only the company can apply for rectification.
misconceptions.correction: The person aggrieved, any member of the company, or the company may apply under s. 59(1).

misconceptions.trap: An s. 59 application automatically suspends voting rights or the right to transfer.
misconceptions.correction: Section 59(3) preserves the right to transfer and voting rights unless the Tribunal has suspended voting rights by order.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 59 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether a name has been entered or omitted without sufficient cause, or whether there has been default or unnecessary delay in entering the fact of membership. II. Establish standing of the applicant (person aggrieved, any member, or the company). III. Identify the correct forum (Tribunal or notified foreign court for foreign members/debenture holders). IV. Seek the appropriate order under s. 59(2) (dismiss, direct registration within 10 days, or rectify depository/register + damages) or under s. 59(4) for contravening transfers. V. Note that transfer and voting rights continue unless suspended. VI. Conclude.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: IRAC-style analysis aligned to the statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions on a Section 59 application contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The register or depository record facts; the ground (without sufficient cause / default or delay / contravention); standing; the precise relief sought (registration within 10 days, rectification, damages, or set-right under s. 59(4)); any interim suspension of voting rights if sought; identification of parties.

examTips: List grounds: without sufficient cause entry/omission; default or unnecessary delay.
Note who may apply and the two forums (Tribunal / notified foreign court).
Tribunal may direct registration within 10 days or rectify depository/register + damages.
Transfer and voting rights preserved unless voting rights suspended by Tribunal order.
s. 59(4) covers SCRA/SEBI/Act contraventions on application by depository, company, DP, holder or SEBI.

enhancement.definition: Section 59 enables the person aggrieved, any member, or the company to appeal to the Tribunal (or a notified competent court outside India for foreign members/debenture holders) for rectification where a name is entered or omitted without sufficient cause or there is default or unnecessary delay in recording membership. The Tribunal may dismiss, direct registration of transfer/transmission within ten days, or direct rectification of depository records or the register and award damages. Transfer and voting rights are preserved unless voting rights are suspended by Tribunal order. Contravening transfers may be set right on application under s. 59(4).
